# Matrix 2026-10: changes from the 2021 public matrix
<!-- SUMMARY: generated by build_matrix.py; every changed cell is tied to a corpus record or attested text; one row added (whomever) · status: built, analyses not rerun · updated: 2026-10-23 -->

Input: `analysis/data/matrix155-lingbuzz.csv` (SHA-256 `a15af082a6bc5dbe24bcf57475c35cad1b00c2dc7e17af584db1841bf7abddf7`), unchanged.
Output: `matrix-2026-10.csv` (SHA-256 `2e329c171a5b50ec3dd8b90a90c378dd8dfba837665fb192195fa9c5aa5951bf`), 139 forms by 155 features, values y, n, and marginal (2 marginal cells).

Rule (Brett, 23 October 2026): a change goes in only if it's linked to specific corpus evidence. The stage-1 proposals that rest on CGEL alone, on Claude's reasoning, or on judgments without a corpus record are held in `corrections.csv`, and so are both proposed new features. None of them is applied here.

## Added row: whomever

Derived from `whoever`'s 2021 row. The changed cells are the ones by which the 2021 matrix separates `whom_rel` from `who_rel`, except where a corpus record says otherwise. All other cells are inherited from `whoever` and haven't been checked separately. Among them is `accepts_genitive_apstrophe_s` = y, which no record attests for *whomever*. Records: `corpus/exclusion_tests/2026-10-17-brett-supplied-whoever-whomever.md`, `corpus/exclusion_tests/2026-10-18-brett-supplied-whoever-whomever-gaps-and-matrix.md`.

| Feature | whoever → whomever | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| whom | n → y | component, as in whom_rel |
| whoever | y → n | component: whomever doesn't contain whoever |
| accusative_case | n → y | as whom_rel; corpus: whomever after a preposition before a pronoun subject, 395 of 802 (17 Oct record) |
| nominative_case | y → n | as whom_rel |
| Monmorphemic | n → n | as whom_rel; whoever is already n |
| appears_in_subject | y → y | corpus: whomever-headed fused relative as main-clause subject, 8 of about 51 (Whomever I chose for this experiment should be close to the mean, Southern Review 2015; 18 Oct record), unlike whom_rel |

## Marginal cells

Coded `marginal`, not forced to y or n. The analyses treat the coding of these cells as a fork (marginal as 0, as 1, and, for distance-based methods, as 0.5), added to the existing multiverse in `analysis/multiverse/`, and report every branch (Steegen, Tuerlinckx, Gelman & Vanpaemel 2016).
